questions.q:
Among the statements
(S1): The set \(\left\{z\in\mathbb{C}-\{i\}:|z|=1\text{ and }\dfrac{z-i}{z+i}\text{ is purely real}\right\}\) contains exactly two elements, and
(S2): The set \(\left\{z\in\mathbb{C}-\{-1\}:|z|=1\text{ and }\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}\text{ is purely imaginary}\right\}\) contains infinitely many elements,
questions.sol:
(S1) \(\dfrac{z-i}{z+i}=\dfrac{\bar z+i}{\bar z-i}\Rightarrow(z-i)(\bar z-i)=(z+i)(\bar z+i)\Rightarrow z+\bar z=0\), so \(z=iy\) with \(|y|=1\). But \(z=i\) is excluded and \(z=-i\) makes the expression undefined: the set is empty. (S1) is false.
(S2) \(\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}+\dfrac{\bar z-1}{\bar z+1}=0\Rightarrow z\bar z=1\), true for every point of the unit circle except \(z=-1\): infinitely many. Only (S2) is correct.

questions.q: If \(z\) is a complex number, then the number of common roots of the equations \(z^{1985}+z^{100}+1=0\) and \(z^3+2z^2+2z+1=0\), is equal to:
questions.sol:

questions.q: Let \(a\ne b\) be two non-zero real numbers. Then the number of elements in the set \(X=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Re}(az^2+bz)=a\) and \(\operatorname{Re}(bz^2+az)=b\}\) is equal to
questions.sol:
Put \(z=x+iy\): \(a(x^2-y^2)+bx=a\) and \(b(x^2-y^2)+ax=b\).
Subtracting: \((a-b)(x^2-y^2-x)=a-b\Rightarrow x^2-y^2-x=1\). Adding: \((a+b)(x^2-y^2+x)=a+b\Rightarrow x^2-y^2+x=1\) (for \(a+b\ne0\), as intended).
Then \(x=0\) and \(-y^2=1\), impossible. So \(X\) has \(0\) elements.

questions.q:
For two non-zero complex numbers \(z_1\) and \(z_2\), if \(\operatorname{Re}(z_1z_2)=0\) and \(\operatorname{Re}(z_1+z_2)=0\), then which of the following are possible?
(A) \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1)>0\) and \(\operatorname{Im}(z_2)>0\)
(B) \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1)<0\) and \(\operatorname{Im}(z_2)>0\)
(C) \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1)>0\) and \(\operatorname{Im}(z_2)<0\)
(D) \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1)<0\) and \(\operatorname{Im}(z_2)<0\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Let \(z_1=a+ib\), \(z_2=-a+ic\). \(\operatorname{Re}(z_1z_2)=-a^2-bc=0\Rightarrow bc=-a^2\).
If \(a\ne0\), \(bc<0\): the imaginary parts have opposite signs. (If \(a=0\), one of \(b,c\) must be \(0\), giving a real/zero part case, not A or D.) So only B and C are possible.

questions.q: If the real part of the complex number \((1-\cos\theta+2i\sin\theta)^{-1}\) is \(\dfrac15\), for \(\theta\in(0,\pi)\), then the value of the integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^\theta\sin x\,dx\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Real part \(=\dfrac{1-\cos\theta}{(1-\cos\theta)^2+4\sin^2\theta}=\dfrac15\). Dividing by \(1-\cos\theta\): \(5=(1-\cos\theta)+4(1+\cos\theta)\Rightarrow\cos\theta=0\), \(\theta=\tfrac\pi2\).
\(\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin x\,dx=1\).

\(u=\dfrac{(2x+i(2y+1))(x-i(y-k))}{x^2+(y-k)^2}\): \(\operatorname{Re}u=\dfrac{2x^2+(2y+1)(y-k)}{D},\ \operatorname{Im}u=\dfrac{x(1+2k)}{D}\).
Curve: \(2x^2+(2y+1)(y-k)+x(1+2k)=x^2+(y-k)^2\). At \(x=0\): \((y-k)(y+1+k)=0\Rightarrow y=k\) or \(y=-1-k\).
\(PQ=2k+1=5\Rightarrow k=2\).

questions.q: The least positive integer \(n\) such that \(\dfrac{(2i)^n}{(1-i)^{n-2}}\), \(i=\sqrt{-1}\), is a positive integer, is ______.
questions.sol:
\((2i)^n=2^ne^{in\pi/2}\), \((1-i)^{n-2}=2^{(n-2)/2}e^{-i(n-2)\pi/4}\). The quotient has argument \(\tfrac{(3n-2)\pi}{4}\), a multiple of \(2\pi\) iff \(3n-2\equiv0\pmod8\), i.e. \(n\equiv6\pmod8\).
\(n=6\): the value is \(\tfrac{2^6}{2^2}=16\), a positive integer.

questions.q:
Consider the following two statements
Statement I: For any two non-zero complex numbers \(z_1,z_2\), \((|z_1|+|z_2|)\left|\dfrac{z_1}{|z_1|}+\dfrac{z_2}{|z_2|}\right|\le2(|z_1|+|z_2|)\), and
Statement II: If \(x,y,z\) are three distinct complex numbers and \(a,b,c\) are three positive real numbers such that \(\dfrac{a}{|y-z|}=\dfrac{b}{|z-x|}=\dfrac{c}{|x-y|}\), then \(\dfrac{a^2}{y-z}+\dfrac{b^2}{z-x}+\dfrac{c^2}{x-y}=1\).
Between the above two statements,
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.sol:
I: \(\dfrac{z_1}{|z_1|}+\dfrac{z_2}{|z_2|}\) is a sum of two unit complex numbers, so its modulus is at most \(2\): true.
II: Let the common ratio be \(k\). Then \(\dfrac{a^2}{y-z}=\dfrac{k^2|y-z|^2}{y-z}=k^2\,\overline{(y-z)}\), so the sum is \(k^2\,\overline{(y-z)+(z-x)+(x-y)}=0\ne1\): false.

Let \(w=z+2=e^{i\theta}\). \(\dfrac{z+1}{z+2}=1-\dfrac1w=1-e^{-i\theta}\), imaginary part \(\sin\theta=\tfrac15\).
\(|\operatorname{Re}\bar w|=|\cos\theta|=\tfrac{2\sqrt6}{5}\).

questions.q: Let \(S=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z-1|=1\text{ and }(\sqrt2-1)(z+\bar z)-i(z-\bar z)=2\sqrt2\}\). Let \(z_1,z_2\in S\) be such that \(|z_1|=\max_{z\in S}|z|\) and \(|z_2|=\min_{z\in S}|z|\). Then \(|\sqrt2z_1-z_2|^2\) equals:
questions.sol:
With \(z=x+iy\) the line is \((\sqrt2-1)x+y=\sqrt2\); the circle is \((x-1)^2+y^2=1\).
Substituting: \((2-\sqrt2)x^2-(3-\sqrt2)x+1=0\), roots \(x=1\) and \(x=1+\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\).
\(S=\left\{1+i,\ \left(1+\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)+\tfrac{i}{\sqrt2}\right\}\) with \(|z|^2=2\) and \(2+\sqrt2\). So \(z_2=1+i\), \(z_1=\left(1+\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)+\tfrac i{\sqrt2}\).
\(\sqrt2z_1-z_2=(\sqrt2+1+i)-(1+i)=\sqrt2\), so \(|\sqrt2z_1-z_2|^2=2\).

With \(z=x+iy\): \(x-iy=-2xy+i(x^2-y^2+x)\). Real parts: \(x=-2xy\); imaginary parts: \(-y=x^2-y^2+x\).

\(\sum|z|^2=0+1+\tfrac12+\tfrac52=4\).

\(Q\): \(2(x-y)\le-8\), i.e. \(y\ge x+4\). \(P\): disc with centre \(C(-2,3)\), radius \(1\); the line \(x-y=-4\) is at distance \(\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\) from \(C\), and \(C\in Q\).
The point \((3,-2)\) lies on the normal through \(C\) (direction \((1,-1)\)). The nearest point of \(P\cap Q\) is the foot on the line: \(z_2=-\tfrac32+\tfrac52i\), \(|z_2|^2=\tfrac{17}{2}\).

\(\alpha z-\bar\alpha\bar z=2i\operatorname{Im}(\alpha z)=2i(8y-14x)\) and \(z^2-\bar z^2=4ixy\). So \(8y-14x=2xy-56\Rightarrow(x-4)(y+7)=0\).
On \(|z+3i|=4\): \(x=4\Rightarrow z=4-3i\); \(y=-7\Rightarrow z=-7i\) (both keep the denominator non-zero).
Sum \(=(4+3)+(0+7)=14\).

questions.q: Let \(S=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:z^2+\bar z=0\}\). Then \(\displaystyle\sum_{z\in S}(\operatorname{Re}(z)+\operatorname{Im}(z))\) is equal to ______.
Let \(z=a+ib\), \(b\ne0\) be complex numbers satisfying \(z^2=\bar z\cdot2^{1-|z|}\). Then the least value of \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), such that \(z^n=(z+1)^n\), is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
Moduli: \(r^2=r\,2^{1-r}\Rightarrow r=2^{1-r}\Rightarrow r=1\). Then \(z^2=\bar z\Rightarrow z^3=1\), and \(b\ne0\) gives \(z=\omega\) or \(\omega^2\).
We need \(\left(\dfrac{z}{z+1}\right)^n=1\). For \(z=\omega\): \(z+1=-\omega^2\) and \(\dfrac{\omega}{-\omega^2}=-\omega^2=e^{i\pi/3}\), whose least power equal to \(1\) is the \(6\)th (similarly for \(\omega^2\)). So \(n=6\).

questions.sol:
\(z+\bar z=(1+i)z^2\Rightarrow z^2=x(1-i)\), i.e. \(x^2-y^2=x\) and \(2xy=-x\).
\(x=0\Rightarrow z=0\). \(y=-\tfrac12\Rightarrow x^2-x-\tfrac14=0\), \(x_1+x_2=1\), \(x_1x_2=-\tfrac14\).
\(\sum|z|^2=(x_1^2+x_2^2)+\tfrac12=\tfrac32+\tfrac12=2\).

\(5(|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2)=30-4\sqrt5\); \(\alpha+\beta=26\).

questions.q: The sum of the square of the modulus of the elements in the set \(\{z=a+ib:a,b\in\mathbb{Z},\ z\in\mathbb{C},\ |z-1|\le1,\ |z-5|\le|z-5i|\}\) is ______.
questions.sol:
\(|z-5|\le|z-5i|\iff a\ge b\). Lattice points with \(|z-1|\le1\): \(0,1,2,1+i,1-i\); all satisfy \(a\ge b\).
Sum of \(|z|^2\): \(0+1+4+2+2=9\).

questions.q: Let the complex numbers \(\alpha\) and \(\dfrac1{\bar\alpha}\) lie on the circles \(|z-z_0|^2=4\) and \(|z-z_0|^2=16\) respectively, where \(z_0=1+i\). Then, the value of \(100|\alpha|^2\) is ______.
questions.sol:
\(|\alpha|^2-2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\bar z_0)+2=4\). Since \(\tfrac1{\bar\alpha}=\tfrac{\alpha}{|\alpha|^2}\): \(\dfrac{1}{|\alpha|^2}-\dfrac{2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\bar z_0)}{|\alpha|^2}+2=16\).
Multiplying by \(|\alpha|^2\) and substituting \(2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\bar z_0)=|\alpha|^2-2\): \(1-(|\alpha|^2-2)+2|\alpha|^2=16|\alpha|^2\Rightarrow15|\alpha|^2=3\Rightarrow|\alpha|^2=\tfrac15\). So \(100|\alpha|^2=20\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha\) denotes the number of solutions of \(|1-i|^x=2^x\) and \(\beta=\left(\dfrac{|z|}{\arg(z)}\right)\), where \(z=\dfrac\pi4(1+i)^4\left[\dfrac{1-\sqrt\pi i}{\sqrt\pi+i}+\dfrac{\sqrt\pi-i}{1+\sqrt\pi i}\right]\), \(i=\sqrt{-1}\), then the distance of the point \((\alpha,\beta)\) from the line \(4x-3y=7\) is ______.
questions.sol:
\((\sqrt2)^x=2^x\Rightarrow x=0\): \(\alpha=1\). Since \(1-\sqrt\pi i=-i(\sqrt\pi+i)\) and \(\sqrt\pi-i=-i(1+\sqrt\pi i)\), the bracket is \(-2i\); \((1+i)^4=-4\).
\(z=\tfrac\pi4(-4)(-2i)=2\pi i\): \(|z|=2\pi\), \(\arg z=\tfrac\pi2\), so \(\beta=4\).
Distance of \((1,4)\) from \(4x-3y-7=0\): \(\tfrac{|4-12-7|}{5}=3\).

questions.q: For \(\alpha,\beta,z\in\mathbb{C}\) and \(\lambda>1\), if \(\sqrt{\lambda-1}\) is the radius of the circle \(|z-\alpha|^2+|z-\beta|^2=2\lambda\), then \(|\alpha-\beta|\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: With \(m=\tfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2}\): \(|z-\alpha|^2+|z-\beta|^2=2|z-m|^2+\tfrac{|\alpha-\beta|^2}{2}\), so the radius\(^2\) is \(\lambda-\tfrac{|\alpha-\beta|^2}{4}=\lambda-1\). Hence \(|\alpha-\beta|=2\).

questions.q: Let \(w=z\bar z+k_1z+k_2iz+\lambda(1+i)\), \(k_1,k_2\in\mathbb{R}\). Let \(\operatorname{Re}(w)=0\) be the circle \(C\) of radius \(1\) in the first quadrant touching the line \(y=1\) and the \(y\)-axis. If the curve \(\operatorname{Im}(w)=0\) intersects \(C\) at \(A\) and \(B\), then \(30(AB)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
\(\operatorname{Re}w=x^2+y^2+k_1x-k_2y+\lambda\), \(\operatorname{Im}w=k_1y+k_2x+\lambda\).
\(C\) has centre \((1,2)\): \(x^2+y^2-2x-4y+4=0\), so \(k_1=-2\), \(k_2=4\), \(\lambda=4\). \(\operatorname{Im}w=0\): \(2x-y+2=0\).
Its distance from \((1,2)\) is \(\tfrac2{\sqrt5}\); \(AB^2=4\left(1-\tfrac45\right)=\tfrac45\), so \(30AB^2=24\).

Let \(S=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z-3|\le1\text{ and }z(4+3i)+\bar z(4-3i)\le24\}\). If \(\alpha+i\beta\) is the point in \(S\) which is closest to \(4i\), then \(25(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to ______.

\(25(\alpha+\beta)=25\cdot\tfrac{16}{5}=80\).

questions.q: If \(z^2+z+1=0\), \(z\in\mathbb{C}\), then \(\left|\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{15}\left(z^n+(-1)^n\frac1{z^n}\right)^2\right|\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
\(z=\omega\) (or \(\omega^2\)). Each term is \(\omega^{2n}+\omega^{-2n}+2(-1)^n\).
\(\omega^{2n}+\omega^{-2n}=2\) if \(3\mid n\) (five values) and \(-1\) otherwise (ten values): total \(0\). \(2\sum_{n=1}^{15}(-1)^n=-2\). Modulus \(=2\).

questions.q: The number of elements in the set \(\{z=a+ib\in\mathbb C:a,b\in\mathbb Z\) and \(1<|z-3+2i|<4\}\) is ______.
questions.sol: Count lattice points \((p,q)\) with \(1<p^2+q^2<16\). Points with \(p^2+q^2\le15\): \(7+14+14+10=45\); remove the \(5\) with \(p^2+q^2\le1\): \(40\).

questions.sol: \(|z-3|=x\Rightarrow y^2=6x-9\). Chord slope \(\dfrac{y_1-y_2}{x_1-x_2}=\dfrac{6}{y_1+y_2}=\tan\tfrac\pi4=1\Rightarrow y_1+y_2=6\).

questions.q: A point \(z\) moves in the complex plane such that \(\arg\left(\dfrac{z-2}{z+2}\right)=\dfrac\pi4\), then the minimum value of \(\left|z-9\sqrt2-2i\right|^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
The locus is the upper arc of the circle through \(\pm2\) with centre \((0,2)\) and radius \(2\sqrt2\).
The point \((9\sqrt2,2)\) is at distance \(9\sqrt2\) from the centre, and the nearest circle point \((2\sqrt2,2)\) lies on the arc. Minimum distance \(=7\sqrt2\), square \(=98\).

questions.q: The equation of a circle is \(\operatorname{Re}(z^2)+2(\operatorname{Im}(z))^2+2\operatorname{Re}(z)=0\), where \(z=x+iy\). A line which passes through the center of the given circle and the vertex of the parabola, \(x^2-6x-y+13=0\), has \(y\)-intercept equal to ______.
questions.sol:
Circle: \(x^2+y^2+2x=0\), centre \((-1,0)\). Parabola \(y=(x-3)^2+4\), vertex \((3,4)\).
Line: \(y=x+1\), \(y\)-intercept \(1\).

questions.q: Let \(z\) and \(w\) be two complex number such that \(w=z\bar z-2z+2\), \(\left|\dfrac{z+i}{z-3i}\right|=1\) and \(\operatorname{Re}(w)\) has minimum value. Then, the minimum value of \(n\in N\) for which \(w^n\) is real, is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
\(|z+i|=|z-3i|\Rightarrow\operatorname{Im}z=1\), \(z=x+i\). \(w=(x^2-2x+3)-2i\); \(\operatorname{Re}w\) is least at \(x=1\): \(w=2-2i=2\sqrt2e^{-i\pi/4}\).
\(w^n\) real \(\iff 4\mid n\): least \(n=4\).

questions.sol:
Second condition: \(y\le x+5\), a line through the centre \((-5,0)\). For \(z=-5+4e^{it}\) on the allowed arc, \(t\in\left[-\dfrac{3\pi}4,\dfrac\pi4\right]\).
\(|z+1|^2=32-32\cos t\), largest at \(t=-\dfrac{3\pi}4\): \(32+16\sqrt2\). \(\alpha+\beta=48\).

questions.q: If \(x^2+x+1=0\), then the value of \(\left(x+\dfrac1x\right)^4+\left(x^2+\dfrac1{x^2}\right)^4+\left(x^3+\dfrac1{x^3}\right)^4+\cdots+\left(x^{25}+\dfrac1{x^{25}}\right)^4\) is:
questions.sol:
Here \(x=\omega\) (a non-real cube root of unity). For \(3\mid k\), \(\omega^k+\omega^{-k}=2\); otherwise \(\omega^k+\omega^{-k}=\omega+\omega^2=-1\).
Among \(k=1,\dots,25\) there are \(8\) multiples of \(3\) and \(17\) others.
Sum \(=8\cdot 2^4+17\cdot(-1)^4=128+17=145\).

questions.q: Let \(z\) be the complex number satisfying \(|z-5|\le3\) and having maximum positive principal argument. Then \(34\left|\dfrac{5z-12}{5iz+16}\right|^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(z\) is the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the circle with centre \(5\), radius \(3\). The tangent length is \(4\) and \(\sin\theta=\tfrac35\), so \(z=4\left(\tfrac45+\tfrac35i\right)=\dfrac{16+12i}{5}\).
\(5z-12=4+12i\), \(|5z-12|^2=160\); \(5iz+16=4+16i\), \(|5iz+16|^2=272\).
\(34\cdot\dfrac{160}{272}=20\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha=\dfrac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2}\) and \(\beta=\dfrac{-1-i\sqrt3}{2}\), \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). If \[(7-7\alpha+9\beta)^{20}+(9+7\alpha-7\beta)^{20}+(-7+9\alpha+7\beta)^{20}+(14+7\alpha+7\beta)^{20}=m^{10},\] then \(m\) is ______.
questions.sol:
\(\alpha=\omega\), \(\beta=\omega^2\). Let \(z=9+7\omega-7\omega^2\). Then \(z\omega=-7+9\omega+7\omega^2\) and \(z\omega^2=7-7\omega+9\omega^2\) (using \(\omega^3=1\)).
First three terms: \(z^{20}(1+\omega^{20}+\omega^{40})=z^{20}(1+\omega^2+\omega)=0\).
Last term: \(14+7(\omega+\omega^2)=7\), so the sum is \(7^{20}=m^{10}\), giving \(m=49\).

questions.q: Let \(S=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:4z^2+\bar z=0\}\). Then \(\displaystyle\sum_{z\in S}|z|^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(z=0\) is a solution. Otherwise \(4|z|^2=|z|\Rightarrow|z|=\tfrac14\); writing \(z=\tfrac14e^{i\theta}\): \(\tfrac14e^{2i\theta}=-\tfrac14e^{-i\theta}\Rightarrow e^{3i\theta}=-1\), giving \(3\) solutions.
\(\sum|z|^2=0+3\cdot\tfrac1{16}=\tfrac3{16}\).

questions.sol:
\(S:\ \tfrac32\le\left|z-\tfrac32(1+i)\right|\le\tfrac72\), an annulus centred at \(C\left(\tfrac32,\tfrac32\right)\).
The point \(P\left(-\tfrac52,-\tfrac32\right)\) is at distance \(|(4,3)|=5\) from \(C\), outside the annulus. Minimum \(=5-\tfrac72=\tfrac32\).

\(25\left((x-8)^2+36\right)=9(x^2+36)\Rightarrow x^2-25x+136=0\Rightarrow x=8,17\).
\(\sum|z|^2=(64+16)+(289+16)=385\).

questions.q: Let \(z\) be a complex number such that \(|z-6|=5\) and \(|z+2-6i|=5\). Then the value of \(z^3+3z^2-15z+141\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
The circles have centres \((6,0)\) and \((-2,6)\), radius \(5\) each, and the centres are \(10\) apart: they touch at the mid-point, so \(z=2+3i\).
\(z^2=-5+12i\), \(z^3=-46+9i\). Value \(=(-46+9i)+(-15+36i)-(30+45i)+141=50\).

questions.q: Let \(A=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z-2|\le4\}\) and \(B=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z-2|+|z+2|=5\}\). Then the \(\max\{|z_1-z_2|:z_1\in A\text{ and }z_2\in B\}\) is:
questions.sol:
\(\max|z_1-z_2|=\max_{z_2\in B}|z_2-2|+4\). \(B\) is an ellipse with foci \(\pm2\), \(a=\tfrac52\); the farthest point from the focus \(2\) is the vertex \(-\tfrac52\), at distance \(\tfrac92\).
Maximum \(=\tfrac92+4=\tfrac{17}{2}\).

questions.q: Let \(z\) be a complex number such that \(|z+2|=|z-2|\) and \(\arg\left(\dfrac{z+3}{z-i}\right)=\dfrac\pi4\). Then \(|z|^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(|z+2|=|z-2|\Rightarrow z=iy\). \(\dfrac{3+iy}{i(y-1)}=\dfrac{y-3i}{y-1}\).
Argument \(\tfrac\pi4\): \(\dfrac{y}{y-1}=\dfrac{-3}{y-1}>0\Rightarrow y=-3\). So \(|z|^2=9\).

Let \(a,b\in\mathbb{C}\). Let \(\alpha,\beta\) be the roots of the equation \(x^2+ax+b=0\). If \(\beta-\alpha=\sqrt{11}\) and \(\beta^2-\alpha^2=3i\sqrt{11}\), then \((\beta^3-\alpha^3)^2\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\beta+\alpha=3i\). \(4\alpha\beta=(\alpha+\beta)^2-(\beta-\alpha)^2=-9-11\Rightarrow\alpha\beta=-5\).
\(\beta^3-\alpha^3=(\beta-\alpha)\left[(\alpha+\beta)^2-\alpha\beta\right]=\sqrt{11}(-9+5)=-4\sqrt{11}\); square \(=176\).

Let the set of all values of \(k\in\mathbb{R}\) such that the equation \(z(\bar z+2+i)+k(2+3i)=0\), \(z\in\mathbb{C}\), has at least one solution, be the interval \([\alpha,\beta]\). Then \(9(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
With \(z=x+iy\): real part \(x^2+y^2+2x-y+2k=0\); imaginary part \(x+2y+3k=0\).
Substituting \(x=-3k-2y\): \(5y^2+(12k-5)y+9k^2-4k=0\), which needs a real root:
\((12k-5)^2-20(9k^2-4k)\ge0\iff36k^2+40k-25\le0\).
\(\alpha+\beta=-\tfrac{40}{36}\), so \(9(\alpha+\beta)=-10\).

The number of values of \(z\in\mathbb{C}\), satisfying the equations \(|z-(4+8i)|=\sqrt{10}\) and \(|z-(3+5i)|+|z-(5+11i)|=4\sqrt5\), is:
questions.sol:
The ellipse has foci \((3,5),(5,11)\), centre \((4,8)\), \(c=\sqrt{10}\), \(a=2\sqrt5\), so \(b^2=20-10=10\).
The circle has the same centre and radius \(\sqrt{10}=b\), so it touches the ellipse at the two ends of the minor axis: \(2\) values.
